mcq_choices.rationale: Assumes that because the block keeps moving there must be no friction, mistaking constant velocity for the absence of a friction force.
Assumes friction only partially opposes the gravity component since the block is still moving, missing that constant speed requires the parallel forces to be exactly balanced.
zero acceleration requires balanced parallel forces
Assumes friction must exceed the gravity component to explain why the block isn't speeding up, missing that constant (not decreasing) speed instead requires the two forces to be equal.

parts.prompt:
A block slides down a rough incline at constant speed. Along the incline, friction is

A. zero
B. less than downhill gravity
C. equal to downhill gravity
D. greater than downhill gravity

criteria.description: Select the single scientifically correct answer.
required_evidence: zero acceleration requires balanced parallel forces

review_notes.expected_reasoning: zero acceleration requires balanced parallel forces
